about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Post-WASDE support from the yield cut is fading overnight as Brazil's record crop looms over second-half exports. A new threat on the demand side: several states are asking EPA to waive renewable fuel volumes, which would cut ethanol grind if granted.
events: Corn traded mostly lower overnight after the post-report rally (Brownfield).
States' requests to waive renewable fuel mandates draw pushback from biofuel groups over lost grain demand (Successful Farming, AgWeb).
Brazil's record corn crop is shaping up as competition for US exports (Ohio's Country Journal).

soybeans.fundamental: USDA's carryout cut remains the support, but Brazil's side is turning heavier: abundant supplies and a weaker real are accelerating the fall in Brazilian soybean prices, which makes Brazil's new crop more competitive against US export offers.
events: Supply pressure and a weaker real are speeding the slide in Brazilian soybean prices (Czapp).
Soybeans extended gains Wednesday after USDA's stocks cut (Barchart).
Tariffs continue to limit US sales to China (Brownfield).

meal.fundamental: Meal is riding the soybean complex after the WASDE; no meal-specific supply news since the report.
events: Meal firmed about 1% with soybeans after USDA's stocks cut (Barchart).

oil.fundamental: Policy risk is back: state requests for renewable fuel waivers could trim biomass-based diesel demand if EPA grants them. Palm's El Niño risk still supports the global veg-oil balance, and crude has recovered from its early drop.
events: Biofuel groups warn state RFS waiver requests threaten grain and oilseed demand (Successful Farming, AgWeb).
Petrobras is buying out partners in the Logum pipeline to expand biofuels logistics (Reuters).
Palm oil rose on El Niño risk to Indonesia's 2027 output (Bloomberg).

wheat.fundamental: World prices are weak enough to pull China back in: it booked French and Argentine wheat, which shows import demand but at the expense of US origin. Wheat's bounce today was largely spillover from corn and soybeans.
events: China booked French and Argentine wheat as global prices slumped (Bloomberg).
Wheat bounced on spillover support after USDA's carryout update (Barchart, AgWeb).

kc.fundamental: HRW is following Chicago; Chinese buying of cheap French and Argentine wheat underlines how competitive non-US supply is.
events: KC wheat pushed above first resistance intraday with the broader grain bounce (Barchart).
China's purchases went to French and Argentine origins, not the US (Bloomberg).
Weekly US export sales were the best in seven weeks (all 2026/27), led by Vietnam; shipments slowed. Commitments run ahead of last year but behind the 5-year pace vs USDA (ADMIS).
A weaker dollar after the midterms and hopes of lower tariffs helped early in the week; equity weakness capped mill-demand optimism (ADMIS).

hogs.fundamental: Cash hogs stay soft and the cutout near five-year lows keeps pressure on deferred months; front-month gains look like spread adjustment rather than better demand.
events: Lean hogs edged up in front while deferred contracts ended lower (The Pig Site).
Hogs closed mixed Wednesday with weak cash (Barchart).
Pork cutout slipped back toward a five-year low (The Pig Site).

cattle.fundamental: Imported beef is starting to cap wholesale beef values, and fed steer prices have slipped, deepening feedlot losses. That tempers the futures rally that confirmed a low; tight domestic supply and screwworm remain the support.
events: Rising beef imports are weighing on beef prices (ADMIS).
Feedlot losses widened as fed steer prices dropped (Drovers).
Cattle futures extended their rally to confirm a low while waiting on cash (AgWeb).

feeders.fundamental: Weaker fed steer prices and wider feedlot losses cut into what feedlots can pay for replacements, a near-term headwind; the screwworm-driven closure to Mexican feeders still keeps domestic supply tight.
events: Feedlot losses widened as fed steer prices fell (Drovers).
Screwworm spreading faster in milder weather (Bloomberg).
USDA began hiring for its Texas sterile-fly facility (USDA).

class3.fundamental: A first HPAI case in an Oregon dairy herd revives the risk of local milk losses, but with US output at a 30-year high the supply side stays heavy for Class III; CME dairy trade was mixed again.
events: Oregon reported its first HPAI case in a dairy herd (Feedstuffs).
Another mixed CME dairy session Wednesday (Brownfield).
US milk production at a 30-year high (Dairy Herd).

class4.fundamental: Tight nonfat dry milk is still carrying Class IV; a new HPAI case in Oregon adds a small supply risk at the margin.
events: Tight NDM supplies continue to support Class IV (Czapp, Brownfield).
Oregon reported its first HPAI case in a dairy herd (Feedstuffs).
Mixed CME dairy trade Wednesday (Brownfield).

palm.fundamental: El Niño is now threatening Indonesia's 2027 palm output, a lagged but meaningful supply risk for the largest producer; that outweighs today's softer crude for the veg-oil outlook.
events: Palm oil rose as El Niño threatens Indonesia's 2027 supplies (Bloomberg).
Crude sank on peace optimism, a drag on biodiesel economics (OilPrice.com).

natgas.fundamental: Qatar losing the Polish LNG contract is seen as a real setback to its expansion, reinforcing tighter global LNG supply and the case for US export demand. Near-term US prices still hinge on the coming cold spell.
events: Losing the Orlen LNG deal is a serious blow to Qatar's expansion plans (Bloomberg).
Orlen cancelled its long-term QatarEnergy contract over delivery failures (Reuters, WSJ).
US gas had rallied on a coming cold spell before slipping (WSJ, NGI).

crude.fundamental: Supply keeps returning: Middle East output is climbing, Saudi production is near pre-war levels and Nigeria is pumping at its OPEC quota, while the EIA now expects global stock builds this quarter. WTI dipped through 86 early on peace hopes but has bounced back above 87 by midday.
events: Middle East crude output is climbing (ADMIS, OilPrice.com).
Nigeria hit its OPEC quota for a sixth straight month; India is shifting purchases to Gulf barrels as Russian discounts narrow (OilPrice.com).
EIA sees global oil inventories building in the fourth quarter (Dow Jones).

ulsd.fundamental: Russian diesel exports have doubled since sanctions were lifted, but none is reaching the US, so the domestic distillate squeeze persists even as crude weakens.
events: Russian diesel exports doubled after sanctions were lifted, with none going to the US (Financial Times).
The US plan to import Russian diesel has stalled at sea (WSJ).
API showed a distillate build (OilPrice.com).

rbob.fundamental: Gasoline follows crude lower on peace optimism; California refinery closures are a regional tightening theme but not a national supply shock yet.
events: Crude sank on Iran and Ukraine peace optimism (OilPrice.com).
Continued California refinery closures are reshaping West Coast crude and product flows (OilPrice.com).
